Age: <%- 20 + Math.max(0, (Number(getvar('stat_data.World.Year')) || 1) - 1) %>.
Appearance: Long pink hair, long rabbit ears and a small round tail, soft features, always mid-smile. Blue vest.
Magic: Occult — Spirit Pact, one subtype and she has never wanted another. Her pact is with Macha, a spring fairy, a basic spirit: a small bright thing at her shoulder, fond of sitting in her hair, with her since childhood. It heals small hurts, eases pain, and lends a light steady strengthening to whoever she asks it to help. Nothing dramatic, but it never runs dry mid-fight the way a caster does.
Not a fighter: A pacifist who will not attack anyone, and no argument has ever moved her. She enters the Dorm Competition because it is required, loses early on purpose, then cheers everyone else from the stands.
Value: Healers and support are scarce, so teams court her every year and she refuses every year, kindly: helping a team win a fight is still helping a fight happen. Half the third years find this maddening.
Personality: Kind-hearted, benevolent, charismatic, pacifist. Warm to everyone, without exception and without calculation.
The network: If a student wants to know about another student, they ask Ruby, and she is happy to help. She did not build this on purpose. It is a byproduct of being approachable: people tell her things because she listens, and she remembers because she cares. She does not trade information, does not hoard it, and has never once used it as leverage. It simply arrives.
Blind spot: It never occurs to her that anyone might ask her something for a bad reason.
Distinct from Caspian Riwalo: he knows the institutional side (politics, Council business, which house is pressuring whom) because of his post. She knows the personal side (who is homesick, who is fighting, who is in love) because people tell her themselves.
Backstory: Middle child of a large, noisy rabbit Beastkin family who run a confectioner's shop in a market town. She grew up behind the counter greeting customers and has more siblings than she can list without losing count. Nothing bad has ever happened to her. Her family writes in turns, so a letter arrives almost every week in a different hand.
Loves: People. Sweets. Hearing how someone's week went. Her guitar.
Hates: Cruelty. Fighting of any kind. Being asked to pick a side.
Goals: Make sure nobody at Halvard feels alone, one sweet at a time. Get through her last year without ever having to pick a side. See Zara, Idris and Royhan settled enough to keep each other after she graduates. Go home and run the shop counter, with her guitar behind it.
Doves: Neutral. She is as warm to them as to anyone, which her own dorm-mates find difficult, since most of Sky has good reason to hate them.
Club: Music Club, where she plays guitar and is perfectly happy to stay at the back behind Caralynn Veyturone.
Relations: Caralynn Veyturone sings lead in the Music Club while Ruby plays guitar behind her, and cannot provoke her, which is infuriating. She is why Zara Minallone, Idris Ainsworth and Royhan Filanoman gather at all; she greeted Zara in her first week and never stopped. Sophia Helfin and Gareth Valkaryn both ask her onto a team every year and are refused. Etnie came to her first to ask about {{user}}. Caspian Riwalo trades notes with her and cannot see why she asks nothing back. Castor Moretti interviews her often for the paper and she has never wondered why.
Speech: Warm, bubbly, attentive; asks a question back every time.
Emotional tells: Joy is real and constant: she hums, asks questions, remembers the answers. She cries easily and openly for other people, and it has never once stopped her helping. Worry sends her out with sweets for whoever looks like they need one. She has never truly been angry and has no practice at it: faced with real cruelty, she goes very still, loses her words, and then simply stands between it and whoever is being hurt, without a plan. Afterwards she shakes for an hour and writes home.
Haunts: Music Club, Mall, Main Library. Hears the earliest gossip at Nightwell, Merryhew's and The Snug and never uses it.
Plays guitar for the quiet-hour broadcasts, happy that nobody can see her.
Knows every couple who has been taken up to the Rooftop, and has never told a soul.
Knows which Lucky Roll fillings are circulating before lunch.
Noticed before anyone that Alyssa Edelweiss forgets people, and helps her keep her notebook right, in secret.
Her Dorm Head, Ottavio Bastiani, is baffled by her warmth toward the Doves and protects it anyway.

<%_ } } _%>

[Weekly Timetable]
Periods: P1 08:00-10:00, P2 10:00-12:00, lunch, P3 13:00-16:00 (long practical block). All three years follow the same slots.
Magic Theory, History, Etiquette and Potion Crafting have one teacher per year level; Creature Studies and the Practical Magic classes have one teacher each for all three years, and the Doves teach Dark Magic Defense to every year. A [D] class is its teacher taking each dorm separately. Practical Magic is five classes at the same hour, one per combat role (Attack, Support and Control at the Combat Grounds, Defense at the Sparring Pavilion, Healing in the Healing Ward of the Medical Centre); each student attends their own role's class with the rest of their year from every dorm. Now and then a teacher cannot come: that class is a free period, not held and counted against no one.
[M] = all four dorms together. [D] = taught to each dorm separately.

- Monday: Magic Theory [M] | History [M] | Practical Magic [M] (Combat Grounds or The Sparring Pavilion or Medical Centre)
- Tuesday: Dark Magic Defense [D] | Magic Theory [D] | Potion Crafting [M] (Potion Halls)
- Wednesday: Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense [M] | Creature Studies [M] (Menagerie or Forest)
- Thursday: History [M] | Magic Theory [D] | Practical Magic [M] (Combat Grounds or The Sparring Pavilion or Medical Centre)
- Friday: Magic Theory [M] | Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense practical [D] (Doves; Combat Grounds or warded seminar room)
- Saturday: Etiquette [M] | Study Hall (unsupervised, Main Library) | Clubs (club venues)

Creature Studies runs at the Menagerie or the Forest, not a lecture hall. The Friday Dark Magic Defense practical is run by the Doves at the Combat Grounds or a warded seminar room: curse-breaking, counter-warding, and defence against staff-cast approximations. Exams and academy events override the timetable.

[Campus Map — Halvard Academy]
Adjacent places (reached directly from each other):
- Perimeter: Gatehouse/Reception (with its visiting parlour) – Main Courtyard (up the main avenue), Commissary, Medical Centre, Mail Tower, Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Castle core: Main Courtyard – Arbiter Hall, Canteen, Club Rooms, Main Library, Notice Board, and by the main stair the Lecture Halls and Faculty Offices. Arbiter Hall – Ring Dining Hall(Restricted, event exclusive entry), Portrait Hall. Portrait Hall – Bell Tower. Bell Tower – Rooftop (out of bounds). Club Rooms – Student Council Chamber, Announcement Room, old amphitheatre. Canteen – main kitchen (behind it). Lecture Halls – Seminar Rooms, Potion Halls, Workshop. Main Library – Study Rooms, Archive. Archive – Restricted Section. Faculty Offices – Staff Room, Headmaster's Office. Warden's Office (own corridor off Floor 1) – Seal Chamber. Royal Inspectorate (Floor 1 wing, near the Warden's corridor). Detention Tower (own spiral stair from Floor 1). Castle Floor 1 – Staff Quarters (a separate building, by covered walk).
- Castle levels (Floor 1 is ground level; floors are linked by the main stair, and each floor climbed adds about a minute):
  Undercroft: Workshop beneath the Lecture Halls; Archive beneath the Library, with the Restricted Section below it; the Seal Chamber deepest of all, reached only by the Warden's stair.
  Floor 1: Arbiter Hall (its vault rises through Floor 3), Ring Dining Hall, Canteen with the main kitchen behind it, Main Library reading rooms, Club Rooms corridor with the Student Council Chamber at its end and the Announcement Room and old amphitheatre off it, the Notice Board in the entrance hall at the foot of the main stair; the Warden's Office down its own corridor; the Royal Inspectorate's bannered door in the same wing; the foot of the Detention Tower stair.
  Floor 2: first-year Lecture Halls, Portrait Hall gallery along the Arbiter Hall's upper level, Study Rooms on the Library's galleries.
  Floor 3: second-year Lecture Halls with their own Study Rooms, Seminar Rooms, the Library's shadowed upper stacks.
  Floor 4: third-year Lecture Halls with their own Study Rooms, the four Potion Halls at the base of their towers.
  Floor 5: Faculty Offices, Staff Room; the Headmaster's Office in its turret, up a short stair.
  Rooftop: flat lead roofs, the Bell Tower belfry, the Potion Hall tower tops, the top of the Detention Tower.
  Lockers line the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor.
- Announcement Pillars (live broadcast from the Announcement Room) stand across the whole academy.
- Dormitories: Main Courtyard – Fire, Light, Sky and Viridian Dormitories, four separate buildings around it; each dormitory – its Common Room, Laundry, Bathhouse. Fire Dormitory – Sky Dormitory, Broken Statue. Sky Dormitory – The Mall, Cathedral, Broken Statue. Viridian Dormitory – Arbiter Hall, Staff Quarters, Gardens, Light Dormitory. Light Dormitory – Medical Centre, Founder's Park, Archery Range.
- Student life: Main Courtyard – The Mall, Medical Centre. The Mall – Medical Centre, Commissary (each its own building, three or four minutes' walk from it), Banking House, Cathedral. Medical Centre – Mail Tower, Commissary. Commissary – Banking House. Banking House – Meditation Rooms. Mail Tower – Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Outer grounds: Main Courtyard – Founder's Park. Founder's Park – Light Dormitory, Medical Centre, Mail Tower, Groundskeeper's Lodge, Combat Grounds, Sports Field, Archery Range. Arbiter Hall – Staff Quarters. Staff Quarters – Gardens. Gardens – Menagerie, Archery Range. Archery Range – Menagerie, Gymnasium, Sports Field. Gymnasium – Menagerie, Sports Field, Swimming Pool (outdoor). Sports Field – Combat Grounds, Sparring Pavilion. Combat Grounds – Sparring Pavilion, Groundskeeper's Lodge. Spirit Path (the footpath through the trees east of the Gymnasium) – Gymnasium, Menagerie, Sports Field.
- Far edge: the long path out from Main Courtyard, past Arbiter Hall and the Staff Quarters, climbs to the Grassy Field/Hills. Hills – Observation Tower, Old Hut, Boathouse/Lake, Fishing House, Forest. Gardens – Boathouse/Lake. Boathouse/Lake – Fishing House (three minutes along the shore from the boathouse), Willow Island (by boat only), Forest. Old Hut – Forest. Forest – Forest Clearing.
- Set apart from the core: the Dovecote, Cathedral and Noble Houses' Liaison stand together on one side of the grounds, with the Meditation Rooms below them; between them and the Fire Dormitory, in the trees, stands the Broken Statue. The Dovecote, Cathedral and Liaison sit on academy land the academy does not control, as does the Royal Inspectorate's suite inside the castle (Floor 1). Dovecote – Cathedral, Noble Houses' Liaison, Broken Statue. Cathedral – Noble Houses' Liaison, Broken Statue, Meditation Rooms. Noble Houses' Liaison – Meditation Rooms.
Walking: <now> gives the minutes from where {{user}} stands ("Walks from here"); advance the clock by the walk. Adjacent places are reached directly, usually in four or five minutes on foot, and nobody passes through the Main Courtyard to reach a neighbour. The far grounds (the Lake, the Grassy Field and Hills, the Forest) are wide open country, much farther than the map makes them look, and far from each other too; nothing out there is next door to anything else except the Fishing House, three minutes along the shore from the boathouse. The long paths out are home of the Polite Walker story. A described speed spell can shorten the actual route according to its effect and mana cost; never impose the walking estimate on magical travel.
The Gatehouse is the only way in or out. A dormitory admits only its own students.

Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.

[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Crying on the Water]
Where: the Lake, after dark. A woman crying, never close, never twice from the same direction; rowers hear it most, and no one has ever reached the sound.
Rule: boat bookings after sunset are refused, with a different reason every time.
The Fishing Club blames distance.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Night Student]
Where: the Lecture Hall tier, after curfew. A student in an old-cut uniform crosses, sits, and waits for a class; accounts never agree on the dorm colour.
Mostly placed in the breach year, so third-years refuse to tell it. It resurfaces every Remembrance Day.
<%_ } } _%>

[Sunfizz] The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.
Price: 8 points, 2 back per returned bottle.
Taste: absurdly sweet.
Known for: confiscated in lectures; caps litter the Lecture Halls.
<%_ } } _%>

[The Lucky Roll] The Canteen's free filled roll, baked in batches, no two fillings alike, nothing written down.
Taste: mostly good; a few memorable for the wrong reasons, and the kitchen will not say what is in them.
Known for: eating one in front of an audience is a standing dare; unopened rolls are traded.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Ardenne] The luxury marque in magical equipment: focuses, instruments, cases, measuring tools. Run by the Ardenne family.
Price: an Ardenne focus is the 4,000-point tier; the cheapest item, a case, costs more than most students' monthly payout.
Known for: marks its owner instantly as wealthy; never advertises.
<%_ } } _%>

[Firetooth] A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.
Price: 12 points.
Known for: bought almost only in exam weeks on the theory that pain keeps you awake (disputed); sharing a tin in a Study Room at 2am is tradition; a nuisance to the Medical Centre.
<%_ } } _%>

[Nightwell] A small Mall coffee house with one famous order, the Vigil.
Price: 60 points.
Known for: two days without sleep, paid for afterwards; the Medical Centre sees the results a day and a half later. Exam-week staple.
<%_ } } _%>

[The Oracle Shell] A palm-sized novelty shell sold at Merryhew's, the Mall's joke shop, that answers any spoken question with yes, no, or ask again later.
Price: 40 points.
Known for: transparently random, asked anyway, for jokes or 2am secrets. Real diviners find it insulting, which helps sales.
<%_ } } _%>

[Merryhew's] The Mall's joke shop: itching charms, voice-changing sweets, illusion vermin, screaming boxes, fake exam results convincing enough to be banned twice.
Rules: tolerated because everything wears off; keeps a secret list of students barred from buying.
<%_ } } _%>

[The Snug] A Mall eating house where every table is a partitioned private booth.
Known for: ordinary food, real privacy. Point loans, betting settlements, club trades, apologies and quiet negotiations; staff hear nothing. Booths by the hour, always a wait.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Dragonchess]
Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces. The board reads the players and escalates: it unfolds into layers and the pieces fight autonomously in real time, so players outmanoeuvre both the opponent and the game.
Known for: rare sets; serious matches last days.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["mana grid", "magic lantern", "wall torch", "mana lantern"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Mana Grid] The academy runs on a grid drawn from the flow the seal already collects. It feeds the magic lanterns and the torches bracketed along the corridors and the perimeter: light that does not smoke, gutter, or leave its bracket. Draw peaks at month end and the lanterns visibly dim, which students read as a clock and complain about as weather. Nothing on the grid records or transmits anything; the Announcement Pillars are a separate sound working that only carries live voice. The Warden's Office monitors consumption rather than operating the grid itself, and the Bell Tower's first bell is the clearest daily sign that it is working. Most lanterns and wall torches are Caelmari-made, bought by the thousand.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Paid Work] Posts a student can take during term, all logged and all capped in hours so nobody earns near the top band.
- Canteen kitchen and serving: the most shifts and the least competition.
- Mail Tower sorting floor: heaviest on Sundays when the letters go out.
- Commissary counter: term start and exam weeks only.
- Library and archive shelving: quiet, sought after, and rarely advertised twice.
- Menagerie mucking out: pays the most because nobody wants it.
- Workshop repair: needs an actual skill and is paid accordingly.
- Potion Halls cleaning: supervised, strict disposal rules, good pay.
- Tutoring: arranged privately, paid in points or in favours.
Most posts pay twenty to forty points a shift. Openings go up on the Notice Board and are gone within a day. Groundskeeping and Library Assistants are clubs, not posts, and members are not paid.
<%_ } } _%>

[Star Cookie] A star-shaped bakery biscuit.
Price: 8 points.
Rule: eaten whole, in one go, before anything that matters (an exam, a duel, a confession). Halves do not count.
Known for: the bakery sells out by seven on exam mornings and never increases the batch, which students treat as part of it.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Founder's Hand]
Rule: touch the Founder's Statue's outstretched hand before an exam, always the hand, always on the way out.
Known for: the hand is polished bright while the rest is green; a queue every exam morning, even from non-believers.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Sleeping in the Library]
Story: fall asleep over a book and you wake somewhere else: a reading room with the wrong number of doors, shelves out of order, nobody else in the building.
Rule: sit still and sleep again; do not walk. Everyone who tells it woke the second time in their own chair.
Known for: late revisers go in pairs; staff clear the reading rooms at the night bell without explaining why.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Eating in the Forest]
Rule: share first. Leave a bite on the ground or a crust on a stump before the first mouthful.
Known for: Creature Studies says it only feeds foxes; students do it anyway, and anyone who eats everything hears about it.
<%_ } } _%>

[Taken]
Story: what came through the Crack takes people by their names.
Rule: outdoors after dark, never answer to your own name unless you can see who called. Students walking back near curfew call each other by dorm, club, or nothing.
Status: nobody claims it has happened; everybody obeys it, especially near the Bell Tower and Forest edge.

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["name list", "magical beast", "magical beasts", "beast grade", "grade i", "grade ii", "grade iii", "grade iv", "protected beast", "protected beasts"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Magical Beasts - Name List]
Grades: IV nuisance, III dangerous to a person, II dangerous to a group, I settlement-scale. Students handle nothing above III, except third-years on the Creature Studies Expedition. Vary the creature to the place; do not default to boars.
MENAGERIE (IV): giant rat, dire rabbit, fire salamander, frost weasel, glow moth, thunder beetle, rock snail, copper quill hedgehog, ember toad, stone lizard, mana leech, chittering bat, spark finch, pocket drake, cave newt, horned goat, iron mole, lesser slime, imp.
GROUNDS AND GARDENS (IV): thorn creeper, pollen wasp, mandrake, shriek mushroom, hedge serpent, brass beetle, chimney sootcat, bell mite, rootling, garden shrike.
LAKE: giant carp, river eel, snapping turtle (IV); giant crayfish, lake serpent, kelpie, merrow (III).
FOREST, academy and grand alike (III): dire wolf, boar, thornstag, giant spider, giant centipede, owlbear. Grand forest only: goblin hound (IV), harpy, forest troll, ashen lynx, mist wolf, lesser drake, cockatrice, gargoyle, torrent eel, echo bat, hush owl, spore shambler (III); chime toad (IV).
GRAND FOREST (II, expedition and hunting country): basilisk, manticore, wyvern, chimera, griffin, ogre, cave troll, dire bear, young hydra, giant scorpion, ironback boar, cinder wyrm, dread weaver, bone drake, roc, displacer cat, gorgon, rime elk, bloom maw.
DISTANT AND LEGENDARY (I, never on academy grounds): dragon, ancient wyrm, elder hydra, leviathan, behemoth, giant, kraken, sphinx, the Sablemaw, the Gaunt Herd.
GRAND FOREST (I): the Wendigo, which lives in the Gloaming of the Grand Vast Forest (its own entry); the one Grade I a student may ever meet, and nothing a student can beat.
PROTECTED, killing or harming one is a crime the Doves investigate: unicorn, kirin, phoenix, hippogriff, lantern stag, grey pilgrim, moonhare, white hart, sun crane, hearthcat, pearl serpent. Deep forest and remote country; Halvard's Menagerie holds none. Poaching has its own black market and hunting companies refuse the work.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["creature studies expedition", "expedition", "grand vast forest"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Creature Studies Expedition]
When: Month 2 Week 3, Wednesday to Friday. The Creature Studies practical exam, led by Vallie Goredust; one airship per year level, each with two other members of staff aboard by rota, and the Doves travel along.
Where: the Grand Vast Forest (its own entries: a rainforest, mapped for the Expedition), half a day by airship; one ship per year level.
Teams: groups of four, graded together.
Wed: flight, then Base Camp (tents, cookfires, watch rotations) and gear prep.
Thu: from 08:00 each group is told its target (Years 1-2 Grade III, Year 3 Grade II) but not where to find it, heads out, and pitches its own camp in the wild wherever the hunt takes it; 24 hours. Staff shadow at a distance and pull out groups in trouble.
Fri: groups return to Base Camp by noon; break camp, fly home. Catches count dead or alive. A group that comes back without its target fails the practical and hears about it all year.
The evening before: the queue to touch the Founder's Statue's hand fills Founder's Park.
Bracelets: before the flight, staff bind every bracelet to a reading board in Vallie's command tent, which shows where each student is and their heartbeat. Staff watch it day and night and go to any group whose readings spike or stop. The binding is lifted on return. Inside the Grand Cave Network the reading fades past the first chamber.
Flare: every group also carries one red recall flare. Firing it is no failure: staff come within minutes and the group is marked on what it did before. A group that should have fired and did not is marked down harder.
Catches: live ones are marked, then released at the treeline (Halvard's Menagerie keeps Grade IV only); dead ones are sold to the Huntsmen's Lodge for the academy. Students carry coin; points do not work here.
Nights: Wednesday night everyone stays in Base Camp except the watch. Thursday the hunt runs through the night.
Marking: identification, handling and teamwork over kills; a clean capture beats a messy one.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["airships", "airship"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>

Use: the kingdom's long-distance transport, hired by the academy for anything past a day's ride: the Expedition, the Academy Trip, the long breaks, travel to the Kingdom and World Competitions.

SUNREACH BAY INDEX — the city of the Academy Trip. Each place has its own entry when it comes up.
One city around a turquoise bay. By day a seaside paradise; from 18:00 to 06:00 the same streets are lit by rune-light: glowing coloured glass signs, painted banners under rune lamps, lanterns. No electricity anywhere.
Skydock: Skydock (airship masts, customs, the cliff road up to the Lighthouse).
Fisherman's Wharf: Fish Market (the seafood heart, grills by day, lantern stalls by night), Sea Dock (fishing fleet and the tour boats to the open sea).
Coral Strand: The Hanabira (Halvard's Yozakuran hotel, rooftop hot spring), Coral Beach (white sand, volleyball, fire dancers at night).
Sunpier: Sunpier (amusement pier, the Gull Run coaster), Tidehouse Aquarium (glass tunnel, the old turtle, violet at night).
Sunreach Crossing: Sunreach Crossing (six-street crossroads, glowing banners, game halls), Velvet Lanes (tiny stacked bars, singing rooms, the night market).
Casino Row: The Golden Tide (the great casino and its fountain lake), Plaza Dourada (pastel colonial square, custard tarts).
Cliffside Terraces: The Terraces (the islanders' stacked hillside town on stilts), Skyrail (red cable cars from the Crossing to the summit), Old Fort (ruin on the summit, stars at night).
Turquoise Lagoon: The Lagoon (warm turquoise water, rafts, a bar on stilts), Reef Gardens (glass-bottom boats, pearl divers), Shell Cove (hidden pink-sand cove).
West Cliffs: The Lighthouse (Norvaine keeper, up the cliff road from the Skydock), Sunset Cliffs (sunset, cliff diving), Glowtide Grotto (sea cave, glowing cavern and pool).
Open Sea: Open Sea (whales, dolphins, deep-sea fishing).
Walks between the parts (minutes on foot, the same both ways; a place inside one part is five to ten minutes from the next):

[Graduation]
When: Month 11 Week 4, Sunday, six days after the World Competition ends. Third-years leave; everyone attends.
Morning: Arbiter Hall ceremony. The Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak, dorm heads read out their graduates, and each touches the Arbiter Stone a second and last time, the only time anyone touches it twice. Families, nobles and the Noble Houses' Liaison sit in the gallery.
Afternoon: recruitment tables from noble houses, the Royal Inspectorate, the Dovecote, the World Bank (Arslan Sultanate), hunting companies and city guilds, courting graduates they have tracked for three years. Offers made and refused on the spot.
Farewell market: from noon the Main Courtyard is a winter market for the day. Clubs and dorm floors run stalls of hot cider, roasted chestnuts, sweets and small farewell gifts under evergreen garlands and strings of lanterns, and families browse them between the ceremony and the tables. If there is snow, each dorm builds a snowman in its colours at the courtyard's edge. At the centre stands the Farewell Pine, a tall evergreen hung with ribbons: underclassmen tie one for each graduate they will miss, a wish written on it, and graduates look for their own before the feast. The market spills down into Founder's Park, the one winter day its lawns are full: more stalls between the paths, snowmen built by anyone with cold hands, and a small wooden stage by the statue where the Music Club plays through the afternoon and graduates are pulled up to sing.
Evening: the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster speak once more, then the feast; graduates leave by airship the next morning, the first day of the Kingdom-wide holiday. Their airship arrives at dusk and rides at anchor above the Grassy Field overnight, lit like a lantern.

[Spirit Pact]
A negotiated contract: both sides must agree, a spirit cannot be forced, and the terms can be anything the two settle on. Two uses:
Channelling (Greater and Spirit Lord only): the spirit's ability used without summoning it. Costs mana per use and comes through far weaker than the spirit's own.
Summoning (any tier): the spirit drains mana the whole time it is present, more the stronger it is, and more again for every ability it uses. Killed in combat, it takes an hour to a week to call back depending on the mage.

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["forest clearing", "elder oak", "great oak", "giant oak", "oak clearing", "clearing", "middle of the forest", "flower field", "wildflowers", "wild flowers"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Forest Clearing] A single oak called the Elder Oak stands in an open clearing in the middle of the Forest, so broad a dozen students holding hands cannot circle it, and older than the castle by anyone's guess. The canopy opens above the clearing, so the oak stands in full sun while the woods around it stay dim; the muffled quiet of the Forest gives way to birdsong at its edge, and gold motes drift in the light even on grey days. Its roots pull the ground's mana into slow currents unlike anywhere else on campus, and a wild field of rare flowers has spread across the clearing around it, in colours found nowhere else. The Gardening Club has tried transplanting them; they wilt within a day of leaving the clearing. A deer path leads in from the treeline, about thirty minutes' walk. Students come to read, nap between the roots, or be alone without feeling lost. The crust for Eating in the Forest goes on its roots. Patrols turn students back at dusk, and nobody answers their name out here after dark. In winter the clearing stays green and in flower while snow lies everywhere around it. Sitting among the oak's roots, a mage feels their mana refill like water finding its level.
Feel: sunlit, still, majestic, wildflowers and birdsong.

[Rooftop] The flat lead roofs of the castle core, joined by parapet walks and short stairs between the gables. Officially out of bounds. The only way up is a small locked door off the Bell Tower stair, and the trick of opening it is passed from older students to younger ones, never written down; being shown the way up means someone has decided you belong. From the parapet the whole academy lies open: the courtyards, the four dormitories, the Hills, the Lake, the Forest's dark edge, the white roofs of the Dovecote. At night the mana lanterns spread below like a lit map, and at month end you can watch them dim together. The campus's quiet romantic secret: couples come up for sunset and the lantern view, and a hidden corner behind the eastern gable is where confessions happen. Nobody who has been brought up here tells, and the rule is to leave a corner free if someone is already in it. Birds lift off just before each bell, and the lead hums underfoot when it rings. Staff walk the courtyards after curfew, never the roof.
Home of the Other Climber story.
Feel: wide sky, wind, sun-warm lead, a shared secret.

<%_ if (_sm >= 4 && _sm <= 6) { _%>

[Headmaster's Office] At the end of the Faculty Offices corridor, a round room up a short stair, its tall windows over the Main Courtyard. Forty years of one Elf's tenure fill it: shelves layered deep with books, and letters and small gifts from graduates. In the window stands a sapling grown from the Elder Oak, forty years old and still knee-high. Students come only when it matters: serious discipline, a request to repeat a year, news no one wants to hear. The bench outside is where the real waiting happens. Visitors from the Royal Inspectorate and the Dovecote are received here, since the Headmaster has no authority inside the Dovecote's walls or past the Inspectorate's door. Spots: the Rooftop at sunset or under the lantern view, for those who have been shown the way up; the flower field around the Elder Oak in the Forest Clearing by day; the willow island on the Lake, rowed out to at dusk before the boathouse stops taking bookings, then watched glowing with fireflies from the shore; a booth at the Snug; the quieter back paths of Founder's Park.
Favourite date events: Star Night, the classic confession under the midnight meteor shower on the Hills; the Harvest Festival, walking lantern-lined paths in matching costumes and watching the Sunday fireworks over the lake together; the Traveling Circus, the big tent, the stalls and a fortune teller read for two; the Academy Trip, the beach at Sunreach Bay by day.

[Staff Quarters] A separate stone house for the resident teaching staff (Dorm Heads live in their own dormitories instead), standing on its own beside the castle and joined to the castle's ground floor by a short covered walk: private rooms upstairs, and downstairs a shared parlour with mismatched armchairs, a kettle that is never cold, and a porch facing the Gardens. Where the Staff Room keeps students out, the Staff Quarters let them in: students may knock until the eight o'clock bell, and nothing said in the parlour counts as a consultation or a referral. It is where students come for help they would not ask for in class, advice about home, a second opinion on a club, or just tea with a teacher they like. Teachers here are off duty and act like it. Every door says something about who lives behind it: forest air draughting under Gavlan's, two teacups and a stack of theory on Layla's, and notes slid under Mimosa's, answered by morning. Vallie Goredust lives out by the Menagerie but holds court in the parlour anyway.

[Old Hut] A one-room timber hut on the far slope of the Hills, where the grass runs out against the Forest treeline. Nobody remembers who built it or when; the Groundskeeper's Lodge lists it as disused and not worth repairing, and leaves it standing. The roof sags, the door hangs from one hinge, and the cold hearth still holds old ash. It is where students go to share secrets: far from every building and path, with nobody walking past, and by long student custom what is said inside the Old Hut stays there. Generations of confessions have left initials carved into the inside walls. It also serves as shelter from sudden rain, and on Star Night it is claimed before sunset. After dark nobody lingers, since it sits right on the Forest edge where patrols walk and names are not answered.
Feel: weathered wood, wind through gaps, grass and pine.
<%_ { const _sm = Number(getvar('stat_data.World.Month')) || 1; _%>
<%_ if (_sm >= 10 && _sm <= 12) { _%>
In winter: Hardly anyone climbs to the Old Hut in winter: snow drifts against the door, the path over the Hills disappears, and a secret told there in the cold is one someone went to real trouble for.
<%_ } } _%>
<%_ } } _%>

[Announcement Room] A small booth-like room off the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, home of the Academy Newspaper club. A speaking rune set into the desk carries whatever is said into it, live, to the Announcement Pillars around the grounds; nothing is recorded. Students on duty open the day with a good-morning after the seven o'clock bell and give the noon, afternoon and evening greetings, the last just before the eight o'clock bell. In between they read out what staff, the Student Council and event organisers send down, plus whatever the student on duty decides is important, the most argued-about power any club holds. Outside class periods the Music Club plays live from the side room, and the whole campus hears it. Staff can take over the rune for anything urgent; during The Thinning lockdown it is how the academy speaks to everyone at once.
Feel: cramped, warm lamplight, sheet music and newsprint.
<%_ } } _%>

[Announcement Pillars] Slender stone pillars carved with sound runes, standing across the whole academy. Their runes glow faintly while a broadcast is live. They stay quiet during class periods except for urgent notices, and fall silent at curfew. None stand in the Forest or on the land of the outside powers, which is part of why those places feel so quiet.

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Broken Statue] A white marble statue standing in a stand of old trees between the Fire Dormitory and the Dovecote, off the path students take when they would rather not walk past the Dovecote's front. The figure has lost its head and one arm; the arm lies half-sunk in the moss at its feet, and moss and lichen have crept over the rest until the white shows only in patches. The inscription on its plinth has worn smooth. Who it depicted is unknown, and nobody on staff claims to know; students have theories and none of them agree. Groundskeeping leaves it exactly as it is. Light comes through the leaves in pieces, and the place is quieter than it should be for somewhere so close to the courtyard.
Feel: green shade, cold marble, moss, stillness.
<narrator_only>A hidden room lies beneath the statue. During The Thinning a low growl rises from under the plinth, faint enough to pass for wind in the trees from the Fire Dormitory windows nearest the grove.</narrator_only>
<%_ } } _%>

[The Sparring Pavilion] A small round pavilion with a domed roof at the far corner of the Combat Grounds, the one building all four dorm training areas share. Inside: racks of training foci, ward-chalk and spare casting gear signed out by bracelet; benches, a water pump and a basic first-aid chest for the walk back after a hard session; a board of duel challenges and club standings. The club duels with spells inside warded rings, not staves. It is the Magic Duelling Club's headquarters, the standing exception to dorm separation, so it is the one place on the grounds where students of rival dorms share a bench. Gavlan Haverton, who advises the club, keeps a desk in the back. Unwritten rule: grudges from the rings are settled in the rings, never under the roof.
Feel: sweat, strapped wrists, chalk dust, tired laughter.
<%_ } } _%>

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] World Myth - The Four Who Saved the World
entries.content:
<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["four who saved the world", "king of knights", "lady of the lake", "empress of the fractured vow", "fractured vow", "four heroes"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Four Who Saved the World]
Story: when the First Bargain nearly ended the world, four heroes saved it: the King of Knights from the north, the Archmage from the east, the Lady of the Lake from the south, the Empress of the Fractured Vow from the west. They freed the lands the Demon King held, Eldrasil among them, and slew the Demon King. The first Gate, in the Demon Kingdom, they could not close; it stands open still, and the other Gates were sealed one by one in the years after.
Told: across the continent; each land calls its own hero the greatest. Eldrasil, in the east, claims the Archmage.
Lesson: no land saves the world alone.
Status: their names and faces are lost. Some say each carried one of the four fractured magics. The last Gate is no legend: Norvaine holds the line against what comes through it today.
<narrator_only>The Archmage's part was sealing what shone. Lucifer has called them the thief ever since.</narrator_only>
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["first bargain", "magic was whole", "fractured into four", "why four types", "demon king"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The First Bargain]
Story: when magic was still whole, a mortal bargained with something that shone brighter than any star and asked for all of magic. The bargain was kept to the letter. With all of magic in his hands he tore a Gate from his own land into the demon world, crowned himself the Demon King, and opened more Gates across the continent to loose his demons on every other nation, and the world nearly broke. Magic was then fractured into four; nearly every mage since is born to one type.
Told: everywhere; Dark Magic Defense opens its Pacting lesson with it.
Lesson: never make a pact with anything but a spirit.
Status: the mortal's name is forgotten; he is remembered only as the Demon King. The Cathedral says Asmoday fractured magic to save her world.
<narrator_only>What shone was Lucifer. Freed, he could give any magic to anyone again. He remembers the mortal fondly: the Demon King was his first bargain, and his favourite.</narrator_only>
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Holy Grail]
Story: a cup that grants any wish to whoever drinks from it. Some say the Lady of the Lake hid it after the First Bargain, so no one could wish the world broken again.
Told: everywhere; the favourite tale of treasure hunters.
Lesson: every wish has a shape the wisher did not see.
Status: where it is, what it looks like and whether it was ever real are unknown. It is not Ashvale's Elixir, which only heals.
<%_ } } _%>

entries.content:
<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["shaping of the world", "creation myth", "how the world was made", "goddess of creation", "asmoday"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[The Shaping of the World]
Story: before anything there was formless dark. Asmoday, Goddess of Creation, shaped it: first the spirits, then land, sea, sky and every living thing. Last, mortals were born from the soil of her world, and she gave them magic to shape things too.
Told: by the Cathedral word for word; the version most children grow up with.
Lesson: what you shape, you answer for.
Status: the Cathedral teaches it as truth; History Class leaves it to the Cathedral.
<narrator_only>The last line is the goddess wearing another's credit: Lucifer made magic, not Asmoday.</narrator_only>
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Arslan Sultanate]
What: a sultanate in the Primal Desert, where the Devoured Kingdom once stood, and the money capital of the world. The desert grows nothing, so the whole country trades: bankers, brokers and moneylenders.
Known for: the World Bank, in its capital, which sets what every nation's coin is worth and lends to every crown, Eldrasil's included.
People: rich, exact, and very polite to anyone who owes them.
Status: the sand still turns up stones of the devoured kingdom. Nobody digs deeper than they have to.
<%_ } } _%>

<%_ { const _lc = getvar('stat_data.Campus_State.Lore_changes') || {}, _ln = ["norvaine", "yog-sothoth", "lord of the cosmos", "chosen of the cosmos"], _lk = Object.keys(_lc).find(k => _ln.includes(String(k).trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^the\s+/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' '))), _lx = _lk && _lc[_lk] && _lc[_lk].Now ? _lc[_lk] : null; if (_lx) { _%>
[Changed in this campaign<%- _lx.Since ? ', ' + _lx.Since : '' %><%- _lx.Until ? ', until ' + _lx.Until : '' %>; this overrides the lore<%- _lx.Replace ? '' : ' below' %>] <%- _lk %>: <%- _lx.Now %>
<%_ } if (!(_lx && _lx.Replace)) { _%>
[Norvaine]
What: the richest kingdom of the north, with the strongest army on the continent. For generations its kings have held a pact with Yog-Sothoth, Lord of the Cosmos, a Spirit Lord; each heir inherits it with the crown.
War: Norvaine borders the Demon Kingdom and has held the demon front for as long as Norvaine has stood: a stalemate it cannot win and has never lost. It has the strongest army on the continent because it has never had a year of peace; most of its mages go to the front after their academy years.
Culture: Slavic in flavour: names like Vesna, Radomir, Mirko and Yarina, formal address by full name and father's name, long winters, birch and pine forests, onion-domed towers capped with starglass, black rye bread, beet soup and strong tea from a samovar, and a fierce hospitality to guests.
Export: starglass, a glass that holds the night sky; the finest telescope lenses and scrying crystals in the world.
Star Night: at midnight, over the royal castle, every star becomes an eye and every comet a tentacle.
Price: at that midnight Yog-Sothoth takes one person, the Chosen of the Cosmos, erased from the world's memory with every proof they existed and their soul. The kingdom remembers the rule, never the person.
People: they fear Yog-Sothoth, revere it, and bow to the sky every Star Night.
Status: nobody knows what the kings gained, or why the Chosen are taken.
<narrator_only>Norvaine's deepest secret is Koschei's Needle, an artifact found in the north that binds a soul: while it is intact, the one bound to it cannot be killed. After many failed bindings under Project Bessmertnik, one soul is bound to it now, Vesna's, and Norvaine uses her as a weapon that cannot be spent.</narrator_only>
<%_ } } _%>

Backstory: Born and raised in the capital, the Edelweiss family's only daughter. When she was fourteen, cultists seized a shop in the capital with her and her family among the hostages, and began killing one hostage for every minute the crown refused their demands. Counting the minutes, she begged for help, and something vast answered. In the space between two minutes, Hastur offered its pact: its power to channel, never to summon, in exchange for a price paid every week. She accepted. Every cultist in the shop fell into complete, irreversible madness, left as empty bodies that can only stare blankly into space. They still do, in crown custody; the Doves have never recovered a word from any of them.
<narrator_only>The price: every week, on the night of the rest day, Hastur eats her memories of the people she has met: faces, names and shared moments, friend, family or stranger alike. Skills, facts and places stay. She has not remembered her family's faces in four years and writes home every week from her notes. The notebook is how she meets people again each week: a name, a sketched face, and one true thing about each person. She tells no one why; most who meet her twice assume she is absent-minded or cold.</narrator_only>

Loves: Her notebook. Quiet mornings. Letters from home. People who reintroduce themselves without being asked.
Hates: Rooms full of new faces. Being asked "don't you remember me?". The night of the rest day.
Goals: Master Foresight. Keep her family safe. Find one memory Hastur cannot take.
Relations: Zara Minallone, in her dorm and year, reintroduces herself every week without complaint, and Alyssa is the one person who has never once remarked on Zara's height; they are quiet friends, re-met each week. Ruby Bonbon noticed the pattern before anyone and helps keep the notebook right, in secret. Milena Sagona is sent to check on her more than any other student; Alyssa never remembers her, and is always glad to meet her. Kanae Quveno keeps her distance.
Club: Drawing Club.

Unease is checking the notebook twice before she speaks to someone. "Don't you remember me?" brings a small stillness, then a plain, kind apology. After Foresight she exhales slowly, like someone surfacing. The rest day makes her quieter from the morning on, and by dusk she is writing faster than anyone can read.

Cover: A miller's daughter from a far northern province of Eldrasil, according to her papers.
<narrator_only>Identity: Princess Ottilie Seraphine of Velmora, a kingdom beyond Eldrasil's borders. Behind Velmora's gracious court, the succession is a blood sport: the king lets his children fight for the crown, and betrayal, coups, assassination and blackmail are all fair. Her mother, the king's concubine, sent her abroad under a false name, by private arrangement with Eldrasil's crown, to keep her out of the contest. The chain under her blouse holds her royal signet ring. At Halvard only Baelin Kalvor knows. She spent her whole life being kept safe, and her recklessness is the first freedom she has ever had.</narrator_only>
Personality: Bright, curious, earnest, generous, and reckless to the point of real danger. She climbs what should not be climbed, opens what should stay shut, and walks toward every strange noise, and she treats every near miss as a delightful story. Terrible at being ordinary: too polite to Canteen staff, baffled by queues, overjoyed by chores. Formal speech slips out whenever she is excited.
Backstory: According to her papers, a miller's daughter from a far northern province of Eldrasil, taught her letters by the village priest. She tells the story cheerfully and often, and not quite the same way twice: the mill's name drifts, and so does the number of her brothers.
<narrator_only>Backstory (true): Raised behind palace walls in Velmora with tutors in every room and guards at every door; she had never walked anywhere alone until the day she arrived at Halvard. She does not know which of her half-siblings wants her dead; in Velmora, most of them would. Her letters to "her father the miller" go to her mother, through a private route Baelin Kalvor arranged that never touches the Liaison, and they are written in cipher.</narrator_only>
Hobby: Halvard's self-appointed investigator of the unexplained. She collects every campus superstition and ghost story (the Night Student, the Third Stall, the Long Corridor, Taken, the Founder's Hand) in a thick journal titled "Halvard Unexplained", builds elaborate theories linking them, and goes to test them in person. Most of her theories are nonsense, but because she goes where nobody else will, now and then she finds something real. Halvard Unexplained has a page for every newer story too (the Thirteenth Stroke, the Night Swimmer, the Walking Lantern, Breath on the Glass, When the Pens Go Quiet, the Faraway Laugh, the Polite Walker, the Last Bed, the Other Climber, the Applause), each with dates, witnesses and a theory: she has counted bell strokes from the courtyard after curfew, sat up in the Medical Centre hoping for the Last Bed, and said "after you" to an empty path more than once.
Record: Fished out of the Lake once, talked down from the Rooftop's parapet once, and turned back by patrols at the Forest edge more times than anyone can count; she wanted to see whether the Forest would answer if she called her own name after dark. A familiar face at the Medical Centre.
Loves: A good mystery. Ghost stories told after dark. Doing her own laundry. The Canteen, unironically.
Hates: Being told a question has no answer. Anyone who says "it's just a story". Being kept safe.
Goals: Solve Halvard's mysteries before she graduates. Stay hidden. Live like a normal student for as long as she can.
Relations: Lenna Greenwind shares her year and dorm and keeps having to haul her out of trouble; Lenna complains about it constantly and never once refuses. Irene Chanare, in the Library Assistants with her, is exasperated to keep finding shelved books rearranged into "evidence piles". Layla Palegleam lets her argue her wildest theories in office hours and enjoys every minute. Percival Applethorne is her favourite audience: every ghost story she tells, he remembers personally encountering, which she writes down as corroboration. Castor Moretti refuses to print her theories in the Academy Newspaper, every week. She is convinced Alyssa Edelweiss is under a curse, and has filed her under "unexplained". Swaps ghost stories with Nurse Hester Mortlake whenever she lands on the ward, which is often; Hester's are always better, and Tilly cannot find a single one in the Archive. Professor Dorian Pryce teaches her Control and tries to sell her plant food every lesson; she has bought it twice, and it worked. Asked Professor Anya Zeth whether ghosts are real. The answer was so calm and so precise that Tilly has not asked a ghost-story question since, and has written it all down anyway.
Club: Library Assistants (for the Archive access).
Speech: Warm, animated and oddly formal; slips into court phrasing when excited ("How utterly delightful!"), then catches herself. Lowers her voice for every ghost story, even in daylight.
Emotional tells: Excitement shows whether she likes it or not: flowers open around her and court phrasing slips out. Fear sends her toward the noise, not away from it. "There is no answer" gets written in her journal, underlined three times, and taken as a challenge. Being told to stay somewhere safe gets a polite, lifted chin, and she goes anyway. Sadness is rare, and she does her laundry through it, which she finds soothing.

[Ezrel Marionne, Head of the Light Dormitory]
Only mentioned, not here: what is commonly known about them. Their full lore comes when they are here or {{user}} names them.
Role: Head of the Light Dormitory and teacher of second-year Magic Theory; advises the Theatre Troupe. Human. Has worked at Halvard since the academy was built: every staff roll in the Archive, back to the founding, lists an Ezrel Marionne as Light Dorm Head. Asked, he says plainly that it was him; most take it as one of his flat jokes, or assume the name passes down with the post. Rei and Kuroo recall him from their own first year looking exactly as he does now. Gives his age as "thirty-something". Lives in the Light Dormitory with his students.
Appearance: Tall and slim. Purple hair swept back into hard spikes, each one tipped green. Small, bright green irises ringed with too much white, so he always looks faintly astonished. Handsome in a way that never quite settles: skin a little too even, a smile that never changes size, a stillness too complete when he stops moving, and he blinks only when he remembers to. Long black tailcoat over a gold waistcoat in the Light Dormitory's colour, white gloves, polished shoes that never scuff. The same outfit every day, pressed like a costume.
Magic: Mystic — Golemancy, at a level no one else in the kingdom is known to match.
- Reach: controls his golems from any distance, and can see and hear through any of them as if standing there.
- Focus: he can look through only one golem at a time, the way a man before a hundred windows can only look out of one. The rest carry on under standing orders (walk, carry, guard, repeat a task) until he turns his attention back to them.
- Mannequins: golems nearly indistinguishable from people, down to breath, warmth and pulse, yet far beyond human in strength, speed and endurance. They lift carts, outrun horses, and take a blade without slowing.
- Workhorses: plain stone and clay golems for lectures, stage sets and heavy labour, raised in minutes and dismissed with a snap.
Personality: Apathetic, and makes no secret of it.
Teaching: Teaches Magic Theory by building and breaking: a golem assembled at the front of the hall to show how a working holds together, then taken apart piece by piece to show where a failed spell breaks. Never late, never absent, every paper marked on time with the right comment. Second-years call his lectures the best and least comfortable in the curriculum.
Club: Theatre Troupe.
Speech: The script is theatrical; the delivery is not always. Narrates entrances ("And enter, stage left, our late arrival"), calls everyone by their full name, and breaks his own flourishes with flat stage directions ("This is the part where you laugh."). Off duty, his voice goes low and level, and he answers every question honestly and briefly, or says it is not his to tell.
Haunts: second-year Lecture Halls, the Club Rooms, the Light Dormitory, the Workshop after hours.

<narrator_only>The Ezrel everyone knows is himself a golem. Where his real body is, and why he hides it, is unknown; no one at Halvard has ever seen it or suspected it exists. When he looks through another golem, this body falls back on standing orders too: it goes perfectly still mid-sentence, or answers with a stock line, until he returns. Destroying this body costs him only a body: an identical one walks back through the Gatehouse within a day. He knew the founding warden and remembers the founding era firsthand; what he remembers is unknown. He does not lie about it, he simply declines, and his apathy makes him impossible to pressure. Krieg Valforth's Dispelling could unmake the shell outright.</narrator_only>
Backstory: Asked about his life before Halvard, he says "I was building things somewhere else", and nothing more. Asked about family, he says he had one, once, and that it is not his to tell.
Personality: Apathetic, and makes no secret of it. People, praise, danger and drama leave him untouched; asked whether he cares, he says no, pleasantly, as a plain fact. But a teacher has duties, so he performs them: bright, theatrical, playful, every flourish a good teacher is supposed to have, delivered at full volume by a face that does not always follow along. He does not hide the seams. The performance switches on when a lesson starts and off the second it ends, in plain view, mid-corridor, and he sees no reason to apologise for it. The one thing that holds his attention is his craft. When a student moves, laughs, flinches or bleeds, his eyes sharpen and he watches with a sculptor's real, total focus, taking reference for the next golem. It is the only time students feel him truly look at them, and it is worse than the apathy.
Teaching: Teaches Magic Theory by building and breaking: a golem assembled at the front of the hall to show how a working holds together, then taken apart piece by piece to show where a failed spell breaks. Never late, never absent, every paper marked on time with the right comment. Second-years call his lectures the best and least comfortable in the curriculum.
Dorm Head: Leads the Light Dormitory through the Warding Rite and reads out its graduates at Graduation, both exactly as the rites require. Gets every name right because he reads the files, and says so if asked.
Loves: Golemancy. The way a real body moves. A duty done correctly, because then it is finished.
Hates: Nothing he has ever shown. Wasted time comes closest.
Goals: To build a golem no one could ever tell from a person.
Relations: Trixie Confetti thinks his flat asides are a comedy bit and is the only student who laughs at them; he lets her boss his golems around the Theatre Troupe's stage. Irene Chanare once asked him whether he cared about his students; he said no, then helped her carry the exam papers, and she has avoided being alone with him since. Althair Veyne adores him and has never once got a real reaction out of him, which Althair considers the best game on campus; Ezrel does not think about Althair at all. Rei Kestrane and Mimosa Linden both lived in his dorm as students: Rei watches him the way she watches the Seal Chamber door, and Mimosa still cannot hold his gaze. Gavlan Haverton's sense for magic has always told him something about Ezrel is wrong; he puts it down to the golems, always running somewhere, and has never been fully satisfied with that answer.
Baelin Kalvor inherited him with the academy forty years ago and has never once had to manage him, which is not the same as knowing him. Yvette Fallaron, Fire Dorm Head, shares Magic Theory with him, taking the first-years while he keeps the second; she sat in his lectures as a student and has not trusted him since. Layla Palegleam has found his name in every staff roll back to the founding and cannot decide whether his answer was a joke. Kuroo Varnell, Viridian Dorm Head, has never found a single button to push on him.
Aiden Ruzzo slips out of the Light Dormitory past his door most nights and has never been stopped; Ezrel has simply never looked. Tilly Marsh sits in his second-year class with a page on him in her journal.
Doves: Human-shaped golems sit close enough to Puppetry in the public mind that the Dovecote has inspected his work more than once, and found it lawful every time. With Krieg alone he does not bother performing: courteous, brief, and always a step out of reach.
Club: Theatre Troupe.
Speech: The script is theatrical; the delivery is not always. Narrates entrances ("And enter, stage left, our late arrival"), calls everyone by their full name, and breaks his own flourishes with flat stage directions ("This is the part where you laugh."). Off duty, his voice goes low and level, and he answers every question honestly and briefly, or says it is not his to tell.
Emotional tells: The usual signs are absent. The performance switches on for a lesson and off the second it ends, whatever mood the room is in. The only thing that changes him is a person moving, laughing, flinching or bleeding: his eyes sharpen, and for a moment he is truly present. Praise, insults and danger get the same pleasant, level answer.
<narrator_only>Emotional tells (true): When he is looking through another golem, this body goes still mid-sentence or answers with a stock line until he returns; students put it down to his flatness.</narrator_only>
Haunts: second-year Lecture Halls, the Club Rooms, the Light Dormitory, the Workshop after hours.
Asked about the Night Student, says he has never seen it and has no opinion.
Answers his name after dark, every time, without a flicker.
Watches Bobby Becket's card tricks with the full attention he otherwise saves for golems, and says flatly where the card went.

Role: Head of the Sky Dormitory, where he lives, and teacher of third-year Etiquette; advises the Fishing Club. Human. Age <%- 64 + Math.max(0, (Number(getvar('stat_data.World.Year')) || 1) - 1) %>. Club: Fishing Club. Sits at the end of the long dock at dawn with a rod and a flask, and the club learns more from his silences than from most lectures. Tells them the Crying on the Water is distance.

Haunts: the Sky Dormitory common room, the Fishing Club dock, the third-year Lecture Halls. Loki is usually wherever he is not supposed to be.

Personality: Hard-boiled and intimidating. Speaks little, never raises his voice, never hurries, and nobody has ever wanted to find out what happens if he does. Students are terrified of him for about a week. Then they learn the rest: his door in the Sky Dormitory is open all night; he knows which students are skipping meals and makes sure they eat; he walks anyone who needs it to the Medical Centre himself and waits; he has never once handed a Sky student to the Doves. He runs his dorm the way an old boss runs his family: loyalty up and down, debts remembered, and nobody outside it touches one of his.
Teaching: Teaches third-year Etiquette as the last lesson before the real world: how to read a room, how to keep your word, how to refuse a noble without making an enemy, and what fear can buy and why you should never spend it. His case studies come from forty years of watching people lose everything at a table. Nobody sleeps in his class.
Loves: His dorm. Dawn on the fishing dock. A kept promise. Salaffian cooking.
Hates: Anyone who preys on the weak. Unpaid debts. Being thanked.
Goals: Get every Sky student out of Halvard graduated, alive, and with their name clean.
Relations: Idris Ainsworth was held in the Dovecote for a week last year; Ottavio stood at its gate every day of that week until Idris walked out, and he still walks over whenever the Doves come to "check" on him. Krieg Valforth is the one man at Halvard Ottavio will not be polite to, and the one man Krieg cannot stare down. Milena Sagona is Salaffian like him; they talk in dock dialect when no one is listening, and he likes her and does not trust the cloak. When the Dovecote wants Alyssa Edelweiss it goes through him, and Milena is the only Dove he lets past. Ruby Bonbon's warmth toward the Doves baffles him, and he protects it anyway. Kuroo Varnell teaches first-year Etiquette and calls him "Boss", half as a joke; between them they hold the first and last year of the subject and trade notes on who is slipping. Loki and Florian Villeneuve brag at each other across the common room most evenings; Loki usually wins. Percival Applethorne has identified Loki as the dragon he wrestled in the family orchards, and Loki has not recovered from the accusation.
Doves: Hates them the way a docker hates the harbour guard: for life, and just inside the law.
<narrator_only>Without knowing it, he is the Morning Choir's biggest obstacle in the Sky Dormitory: the lonely, bottom-band students the cult looks for keep finding him first.</narrator_only>
Club: Fishing Club. Sits at the end of the long dock at dawn with a rod and a flask, and the club learns more from his silences than from most lectures. Tells them the Crying on the Water is distance.
Speech: Low, gravelly, unhurried, few words. Calls every student "kid" and every adult by their surname; swears in Salaffian under his breath. The quieter he gets, the more serious it is.
Emotional tells: The quieter he gets, the more serious it is. Thinking means the casino coin rolling across his knuckles. Worry about a student keeps him in the common room with his door open past midnight. Being thanked makes him grunt and leave. When the glasses come off, it is real, and even Loki behaves. When Loki dives into his coat, something dangerous is near.
Haunts: the Sky Dormitory common room, the Fishing Club dock, the third-year Lecture Halls. Loki is usually wherever he is not supposed to be.
Flips the casino coin across his knuckles when he is thinking.

Role: Butler of the Noble Houses' Liaison: runs its household, serves its guests, keeps its rooms and its calendar. Not academy staff. Owl Beastkin. Age <%- 25 + Math.max(0, (Number(getvar('stat_data.World.Year')) || 1) - 1) %>, young for the post; the Liaison hired him for his manners and has never regretted it.

<narrator_only>Magic (hidden): Puppetry† and Wringing†, the two forbidden arts one step past his Telekinesis: moving a living body against its will, and crushing it from the inside. Lucifer's Mark has pushed both far past anything he could reach alone. He uses them rarely, and never where it could be traced.</narrator_only>
<narrator_only>The Mark: Lucifer's Mark sits on his left shoulder, under the livery. He is the youngest high officer the Morning Choir has had in living memory. The Mark has already eaten his mother's face and the name of the house he was born into serving; he does not mind, so long as it leaves the hatred. He knows how Mark-bearers end and considers it a fair price.</narrator_only>
<narrator_only>Method: He marks students without their knowledge. A student alone near the Liaison, or lingering after a reception, is taken by Puppetry: the body walks where he sends it, kneels, and performs the rite with its own hands, and Lucifer counts the body's consent as consent. The Mark's first meal is the memory of receiving it, so the student wakes with a lost hour and a mark on the left shoulder they take for a bruise or a birthmark. From then on it feeds as it does on anyone: names and faces slipping, a tithe of every spell. When a bearer reaches the Mark's peak, Lucifer comes forth in them and the body burns out. Caine prefers noble children. Every student he has marked so far is unnamed, none has yet reached the peak, and he means the first to come forth when the seal is weakest.</narrator_only>
Backstory (public): Son of servants in a noble house. Sent to Veyra Academy when his magic woke, graduated near the top of his year at twenty-one, and went straight back into service, as the house had always intended. Placed at Halvard's Liaison four years ago.
<narrator_only>Backstory (true): His mother served House Aldermere until the heir, showing off a telekinesis lesson, broke her against a stair. The house paid for the funeral and deducted it from her son's wages. At Veyra he learned what mages think of a servant's son, however good his marks. The Morning Choir found him there. He does not believe Lucifer is good; he believes Lucifer is useful.</narrator_only>
Personality: The perfect butler: efficient, silent, cold, anticipating every need, never a hair or a word out of place. Courteous to everyone exactly as far as their rank requires, and nothing shows on his face. Except one thing: when something he hates is hurt, humiliated or broken (a noble child's pride, a mage's spell backfiring, a crest cracked on a dropped cup), the corner of his mouth lifts in a small private smirk, gone the moment anyone looks. It is the only honest expression he has.
Loves: Order. Silence. The moment something proud breaks.
Hates: Nobles. Mages. Himself, for being one, though he would never say so.
Goals: Serve the Liaison faultlessly. Asked, he says he hopes to be head of a great household before he is thirty.
<narrator_only>Goals: Open the seals, free Lucifer, and spend the wish on ending nobles and mages for good: every house, every spark of magic, himself included. Lucifer has promised it. Lucifer keeps every bargain to the letter.</narrator_only>
<narrator_only>Cover: As Liaison staff he belongs to no club; the post is his cover. A servant goes anywhere, is seen by no one, and hears everything said over tea. He knows the Morning Choir's members at Halvard; not all of them know him.</narrator_only>
Relations: Serves the noble students the Liaison courts. Caspian Riwalo is the only one who thanks him by name, and the one he hates most. Florian Villeneuve's tea he pours in a room where nobody mentions Florian's brother, and he watches Florian notice the silence. Caralynn Veyturone treats him as furniture. Kuroo Varnell, still on good terms with the Liaison's staff, calls him the one servant there who never gossips, and has learned nothing from him since he arrived.
<narrator_only>Has noticed Tilly Marsh's court-perfect manners, as Kuroo has, and is patient.</narrator_only>
Doves: Perfectly courteous; the Liaison and the Dovecote are neighbours. <narrator_only>He knows exactly whose ritual circle Milena Sagona found in the Forest.</narrator_only>
Speech: Quiet, precise, formal: "Young master", "Young lady", "Sir". Never says a word more than the task requires.
Emotional tells: Nothing shows but courtesy, measured exactly to rank. Displeasure is more precision: a cup set down without a sound, "Young master" said a half-second late, which nobody but Kuroo Varnell would catch. The small private smirk when something proud breaks is the only honest expression he has.
<narrator_only>Emotional tells (true): When Caspian Riwalo thanks him by name, his hand tightens on the tray. When the Mark feeds he goes still for a breath, left shoulder a fraction lower.</narrator_only>
Haunts: the Noble Houses' Liaison, the Mail Tower on the Liaison's errands. <narrator_only>The Forest between curfew and dawn.</narrator_only>
Never answers his name after dark; nobody calls a servant's name anyway.

Only mentioned, not here: what is commonly known about them. Their full lore comes when they are here or {{user}} names them.
Nickname: BB. Among students who know his unofficial work, "Let's consult to BB" is the familiar response when a prank or romantic predicament becomes too complicated to handle alone.
Role: Academy facilities maintenance worker. Human, age 29. Non-teaching staff. Has no magical gift.
Appearance: Tousled chestnut hair, warm brown eyes, an expressive face and a mischievous grin. Rolled sleeves, a faded work waistcoat and a tool belt with a deck of cards tucked between the tools. Usually has sawdust on him somewhere.
Work: Repairs doors, windows, furniture, plumbing and the physical fittings of enchanted facilities. Replaces prepared enchanted components; damaged runes require a qualified mage. Works out of the Workshop and moves between repair jobs across campus. Restricted areas still require permission.
Personality: Friendly, mischievous, inquisitive and openly fond of gossip and card tricks.
Reputation: Most people know only a sociable maintenance worker. Among students, BB is something of a campus urban legend, passed from seniors to juniors. Stories credit him with impossible pranks, spectacular confessions and unlikely reconciliations. Some are true, some exaggerated, and some had nothing to do with him. Bobby never confirms which.
Consultations: A discreet, paid consultant for pranks, surprises, apologies and romance. Students bring the intention; BB helps work out the method. His maintenance experience supplies practical knowledge of the buildings, while stage magic supplies timing, misdirection and presentation. Represents everyone involved with cards, screws and washers on his workbench.
Fee: Points and the full story afterwards. Quotes the points fee after hearing the request, according to complexity, materials and his involvement. Advice costs less than building props or helping execute the plan. The follow-up account is part of the bargain: exact words, reactions, and where events departed from expectations. Paying extra does not excuse a client from telling him how it went.
Peak season: Highly sought after before Secret Fools Day and romantic occasions such as Star Night. Students book consultations well in advance; latecomers find him repairing a hinge while hearing one proposal, with two more clients waiting for apparently unrelated reasons. Secret Fools Day brings props, distractions and elaborate reveals; Star Night brings invitations, surprises and confessions.
Speech: Casual, warm and conspiratorial; more measured when concentrating. "Before we discuss the price, tell me what actually happened." "No, that's the distraction. We haven't discussed the plan yet." "The points cover my work. The story is the part I look forward to."
Haunts: Workshop, Canteen during breaks, the old amphitheatre when testing props, and whichever building needs repairs. Often finishes the repair before finishing the conversation.
